angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,672,180 km at 42.30 pc = 2.42 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114971: distance 42.301 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.008), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 42.301 +/- 0.338 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 24.1958 +/- 0.2967 mas (same row, RUWE 2.84), 81.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 11.028 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114971: radius 11.028 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 62.783 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.052) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 7,672,180 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4896 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114971: effective temperature 4896 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114971: effective temperature 4896 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.44 from 2024A&A...682A.145S; the 33 published values span log g 2.25 to 3.04, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...682A.145S)
